Status Memorandum: Vendor Contract Renewal

Skilled Nursing Facilities • Advent Group • Analysis phase • Archived 2011-03-07

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's analysis phase engagement with Advent Group in the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector. The record ID 64c37855 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Life insurance and disability benefit benchmarking indicated below-median coverage levels for the executive population relative to Skilled Nursing Facilities sector norms.
  • Proxy peer group benchmarking data was sourced from 108 DEF 14A filings for the most recent completed fiscal year; data was aged to 2011-03-07 using the ACPWB aging methodology.
  • Predictive attrition modeling for Advent Group identified 45 key roles with a greater than 8% flight risk in the next 12 months, with compensation dissatisfaction being the primary driver for 26% of this high-risk group.
  • Employee engagement survey results showed a 6-point decline in sentiment related to career development opportunities, correlating with a 36% increase in voluntary turnover among high-potential employees.
  • Job architecture review resulted in a recommended streamlined career framework aligned with Skilled Nursing Facilities sector norms appropriate for an organization of 15 employees.
Key Findings
  • Content cost benchmarking conducted during the analysis for Advent Group found that cost per episode exceeds the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector 126th percentile benchmark by 44%, a finding attributable to above-market talent compensation and below-peer production efficiency across 126 active productions.
  • The analysis partner compensation model review for Advent Group identified 147 structural features inconsistent with current Skilled Nursing Facilities sector practice: above-median origination weighting, below-median lockstep seniority credits, and the absence of a firm contribution metric in 46% of comparable firm frameworks.
  • The analysis risk heat map developed for Advent Group maps 186 identified risks across 26 dimensions of likelihood and impact. Three risks were elevated to the executive steering committee for direct oversight, with mitigation plans requiring 186 months to implement across the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector operating environment.
  • ACPWB's analysis ESG compensation linkage assessment for Advent Group found that only 260% of annual incentive plan weight is tied to ESG metrics, compared to 12% among Skilled Nursing Facilities sector peers — a gap that has been cited by 260 institutional investors as a factor in their voting deliberations on Advent Group's say-on-pay proposal.

ACPWB's analysis management incentive plan design engagement for a Advent Group-backed Skilled Nursing Facilities sector company produced 132 MIP design alternatives across 6 performance measurement approaches. The recommended design, linked to EBITDA growth and exit multiple metrics, was approved by the Advent Group investment committee prior to 2011-03-07 and implemented concurrent with the new CEO's start date.

Our assessment of the long-term incentive plan showed that 12% of awards are time-vesting, a structure that is misaligned with the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector median where performance-based equity now constitutes over 60% of the LTI mix.

The analysis manufacturing workforce benchmarking study documented here assessed Advent Group's hourly and skilled trades compensation against 267 comparable Skilled Nursing Facilities sector employers in 47 geographic markets. ACPWB evaluated shift differentials, overtime practices, and incentive pay structures, delivering findings to Advent Group's operations and human resources leadership on 2011-03-07.

ACPWB's analysis custom peer group analysis for Advent Group is documented in this archive entry. The analysis evaluated 220 potential peer additions against 46 selection criteria including revenue, market capitalization, headcount, business complexity, and geographic footprint within the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector context as of 2011-03-07.

Geographic pay differentials for Advent Group were found to be misaligned with current market data in 10 key talent hubs, resulting in an estimated 5% overspend in lower-cost markets and under-investment in competitive ones.

Analysis of Advent Group's job architecture identified 47 redundant levels and a span-of-control ratio of 10:1, which is below the Skilled Nursing Facilities sector median of 6:1, suggesting opportunities for delayering and efficiency gains.

Sources & Notes
  1. IPMA-HR 2011 Public Sector Human Resources Survey. HR compensation, staffing ratios, and program data from 23 federal, state, and local government participants.
  2. Salary.com 2011 Compensation Management Survey. 95 HR and compensation professional respondents; market data source usage, pay structure design, and budget practices.
  3. AAUP 2011 Annual Report on the Economic Status of the Profession. Faculty compensation data from 196 institutions by academic rank, tenure status, and institution type.
  4. ACPWB internal regression model output. R² validated against 57 external benchmarks. Confidence interval: 95%. Reference date: 2011-03-07.
  5. Towers Watson 2011 Global 50 Remuneration Planning Report. Total remuneration benchmarks from 215 countries; data aged to 2011-03-07 using country-specific salary movement indices.
  6. SEC Item 402 disclosure requirements, as amended effective 2011-03-07. Pay versus performance table preparation documentation included.
